• Release epinephrine/norepinephrine directly into the bloodstream upon preganglionic stimulation.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: During the fifth week of gestation, the primary acidophilic cell mass that forms the fetal cortex is derived from [___] cells.
back:
• Mesothelial cells (Mesoderm).
• Proliferate between the mesentery and urogenital ridge.
• Represent the first stage of cortical development.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A patient presents with paroxysmal hypertension and tachycardia. If the tumor involves neural crest derivatives in the adrenal gland, identify the cell type and hormone involved.
back:
• Cell type: Chromaffin cells (Medulla).
• Condition: Pheochromocytoma.
• Hormones: Epinephrine and Norepinephrine (Catecholamines).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Describe the molecular signaling mechanism provided by the dorsal aorta that facilitates adrenal medulla formation.
back:
• Secretes Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs).
• BMPs act as chemoattractants for neural crest cells.
• Regulates the specification and migration of crest cells into the gland.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Germ Layer Duality of Adrenal Gland
front: Contrast the germ layer origins and hormonal products of the adrenal cortex versus the adrenal medulla.
back:
• Cortex: Mesoderm; produces Steroids (Cortisol, Aldosterone, Androgens).
• Medulla: Ectoderm (Neural Crest); produces Catecholamines (Epinephrine).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Identify the three definitive cortical layers that differentiate from the second mesothelial wave shortly after birth.
back:
• Zona glomerulosa (Outer).
• Zona fasciculata (Middle).
• Zona reticularis (Inner).

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Embryological origin of the fetal adrenal cortex
front: The fetal (primitive) adrenal cortex is derived from the first wave of large acidophilic cells originating from the [___].
back:
Mesothelium (Mesoderm)
- Located between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Germ layer origin of adrenal steroidogenic tissue
front: A neonate presents with ambiguous genitalia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Identify the embryological germ layer responsible for the pathological steroid-producing tissue.
back:
Mesoderm
- Specifically the second wave of mesothelial cells.
- These form the definitive adrenal cortex.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Molecular regulation of adrenal medulla development
front: Explain the role of Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs) secreted by the dorsal aorta in adrenal development.
back:
Regulation of Neural Crest Cells:
- Signals the migration of neural crest cells toward the adrenal primordium.
- Induces specification into chromaffin cells.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Dual embryological origin of the adrenal gland
front: Contrast the embryological lineage and functional classification of chromaffin cells versus the definitive adrenal cortex.
back:
Chromaffin Cells:
- Ectoderm (Neural crest).
- Modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons.
Definitive Cortex:
- Mesoderm (Mesothelium).
- Steroid-producing epithelial cells.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Endocrine function of the fetal adrenal cortex
front: Identify the specific steroid precursor secreted by the fetal cortex that is essential for placental estrogen synthesis.
back:
Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)
- Secreted in the second trimester.
- Converted to estrogen by the placenta to maintain pregnancy.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Congenital tumors of the adrenal medulla arising from neural crest remnants that produce excess catecholamines are known as [___].
back:
Pheochromocytomas
- Involve chromaffin cells.
- Often associated with RET gene mutations.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: A histological section of a neonatal adrenal gland shows rapid involution of the internal acidophilic zone. Describe the normal embryological fate of this layer.
back:
Fetal (Primitive) Cortex Regression:
- Occurs rapidly after birth.
- Replaced by differentiating layers of the definitive cortex.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Neural crest migration in adrenal development
front: Describe the migratory path of the precursors for the adrenal medulla during the fifth week of development.
back:
Neural Crest Migration:
- Cells leave the neural folds.
- Invade the medial aspect of the mesodermal cortical primordium.
- Arrange into cords and clusters.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Distinguish the origin of the three definitive cortical layers (glomerulosa, fasciculata, reticularis) from the fetal adrenal cortex.
back:
Definitive Layers:
- From a second wave of smaller mesothelial cells.
- Surrounds the acidophilic fetal mass.
- Differentiates fully after birth.

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Identify the primary source of epinephrine and norepinephrine in the embryo.
back:
Chromaffin Cells
- Derived from ectodermal neural crest.
- Distributed widely in embryos; restricted to adrenal medulla in adults.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: The fetal (primitive) cortex of the adrenal gland is primarily derived from [___] cells that proliferate during the fifth week of development.
back:
• Mesothelial cells (Mesoderm)
• Located between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A 40-year-old male presents with paroxysmal hypertension, palpitations, and headaches. A CT scan reveals a mass in the adrenal medulla. Identify the specific embryonic cell type involved.
back:
• Chromaffin cells
• Derived from Neural Crest cells (Ectoderm).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Endocrine Function of Fetal Adrenal Cortex
front: Explain the physiological role of the fetal adrenal cortex in maintaining pregnancy via its interaction with the placenta.
back:
• Secretes DHEA (Dehydroepiandrosterone)
• Converted to estrogen by the placenta
• Estrogen maintains the pregnancy and placental function.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Dual Origin of the Adrenal Gland
front: Contrast the embryonic origin and functional identity of the adrenal cortex versus the adrenal medulla.
back:
• Cortex: Mesothelial mesoderm; produces steroids (cortisol, aldosterone).
• Medulla: Neural crest ectoderm; functions as modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: List the three definitive layers of the adrenal cortex that differentiate from the second mesothelial wave after the fetal cortex regresses postnatally.
back:
• Zona glomerulosa
• Zona fasciculata
• Zona reticularis.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Molecular Regulation of Adrenal Medulla Development
front: The migration and specification of neural crest cells into the adrenal medullary mass are primarily regulated by [___] secreted by the dorsal aorta.
back: • Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: An infant with ambiguous genitalia is diagnosed with 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Explain the embryological consequence for the adrenal gland in this condition.
back:
• Results in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH)
• Causes excessive production of androgens by the definitive cortex.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: How do the 'two waves' of mesothelial cell proliferation differ in their contribution to the adrenal cortical structure?
back:
• 1st Wave: Forms the large, acidophilic fetal (primitive) cortex.
• 2nd Wave: Forms the definitive cortex that persists after birth.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Distinguish between the postnatal fate of the fetal cortex and the definitive cortex.
back:
• Fetal Cortex: Regresses rapidly after birth.
• Definitive Cortex: Persists and differentiates into three histological zones.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Identify the specific neurotransmitters released into the bloodstream by the adrenal medullary cells upon stimulation by preganglionic sympathetic fibers.
back:
• Epinephrine (Adrenaline)
• Norepinephrine (Noradrenaline).

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Embryological origin of the adrenal medulla
front: The adrenal medulla is embryologically derived from [___] cells, which also give rise to the dorsal root and sympathetic ganglia.
back: "• Neural crest cells\n• They migrate from the neural folds during the fifth week\n• Differentiate into chromaffin cells."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: A female newborn presents with ambiguous genitalia and clitoral hypertrophy. Lab studies reveal 21-hydroxylase deficiency. Identify the embryological source of the affected organ tissue.
back: "• Mesoderm (mesothelial cells)\n• Located between the root of mesentery and the urogenital ridge\n• Results in excessive androstenedione production."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: Functional role of the fetal cortex
front: Explain the role of the fetal adrenal cortex in maintaining a healthy pregnancy through its interaction with the placenta.
back: "• Secretes Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)\n• Placenta converts fetal DHEA into estrogens\n• Essential for maintaining the pregnancy environment."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Contrast the developmental fate of the fetal (primitive) cortex with that of the definitive adrenal cortex.
back: "• Fetal cortex: Large acidophilic cells; regresses rapidly after birth\n• Definitive cortex: Smaller mesothelial cells; differentiates into three adult layers."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Name the specific molecular signaling proteins secreted by the dorsal aorta that act as chemoattractants for migrating neural crest cells during medullary development.
back: "• Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs)\n• Direct crest cells to the medial aspect of the cortex."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: The [___] cells of the adrenal medulla represent modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons that release hormones directly into the bloodstream.
back: "• Chromaffin cells\n• Innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers\n• Produce epinephrine and norepinephrine."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
coreConcept: RET gene in neural crest development
front: A patient is diagnosed with a rare tumor of the adrenal medulla (Pheochromocytoma) and found to have a RET gene mutation. Relate this mutation to adrenal development.
back: "• RET gene is essential for neural crest migration\n• Mutations predispose to chromaffin cell tumors and Hirschsprung disease."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Describe the histological transition of the adrenal cortex that occurs immediately after birth.
back:
"• Massive regression of the acidophilic fetal zone
• Differentiation of definitive cortex into: 
• Zona glomerulosa
• Zona fasciculata
• Zona reticularis."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Distinguish the origin of the fetal adrenal cortex from the origin of the definitive adrenal cortex.
back: "• Fetal: First wave of mesothelial cells between mesentery and gonad\n• Definitive: Second wave of mesothelial cells surrounding the fetal mass."

category: Describe the embryological basis for the congenital anomalies of adrenal development
front: Where specifically does the adrenal cortex primordium first appear during the fifth week of development?
back: "• In the mesenchyme\n• Between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad."

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Gonads initially appear as a pair of longitudinal elevations formed by epithelial proliferation and mesenchymal condensation known as [___].
back:
• Genital (or gonadal) ridges.
• Appear before the 7th week.
• Formed medially to the mesonephros.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: Inductive Influence of Primordial Germ Cells
front: A fetus fails to develop gonads despite a normal 46,XX karyotype. Histology reveals an absence of germ cells in the genital area. This condition arises because [___] failed to reach the genital ridges.
back:
• Primordial germ cells (PGCs).
• PGCs have an essential inductive influence on gonadal development.
• Without PGCs, gonads remain rudimentary or absent.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Describe the specific migratory path of primordial germ cells from their 3rd-week residence to the primitive gonads.
back:
• Origin: Epiblast.
• 3rd week: Wall of the yolk sac near the allantois.
• 4th week: Ameboid movement along the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut.
• 5th/6th week: Invade the genital ridges.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the indifferent gonad's 'primitive sex cords' with the 'cortical cords' of the developing ovary.
back:
• Primitive Sex Cords: Found in both sexes; connected to surface epithelium.
• Cortical Cords: Second generation of cords; unique to females; appear in the 7th week after medullary cords dissociate.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Identify the specific cell type and embryological origin that forms the 'primitive sex cords' in the indifferent stage.
back:
• Surface epithelium of the genital ridge.
• Proliferating epithelial cells penetrate the underlying mesenchyme.
• Occurs shortly before the arrival of primordial germ cells.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Primordial germ cells are derived from the [___] before they migrate to the wall of the yolk sac.
back:
• Epiblast.
• They migrate through the primitive streak.
• This occurs during the 3rd week of development.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A 6-week-old embryo is examined. Regardless of genetic sex, it possesses both mesonephric and paramesonephric ducts. This period is referred to as the [___].
back:
• Indifferent stage of the genital system.
• Sex-specific morphological characteristics only appear starting in the 7th week.
• Genetic sex is determined at fertilization, but phenotypic expression is delayed.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain the role of the 'urogenital ridge' and specify its two major anatomical subdivisions.
back:
• Formed by the large ovoid mesonephros and the developing gonad.
• Medial portion: Genital ridge (forms gonads).
• Lateral portion: Mesonephric ridge (forms urinary units).

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the structural fate of primitive sex cords in male vs. female embryos.
back:
• Males (XY): Persist and proliferate into medullary (testis) cords under SRY influence.
• Females (XX): Dissociate into irregular cell clusters and eventually disappear in the medulla.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: State the chronological milestone by which primordial germ cells must invade the genital ridges to ensure gonadal development.
back:
• By the 6th week of development.
• They arrive at the primitive gonads at the beginning of the 5th week.
• Failure to reach the ridges results in gonadal agenesis.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: The adrenal medulla is embryologically derived from [___] cells that migrate into the medial aspect of the developing gland.
back:
● Neural crest cells
● These differentiate into chromaffin cells
● Functionally represent modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A newborn exhibits rapid regression of a specific adrenal layer shortly after birth. This layer was primarily responsible for secreting [___] during fetal life.
back:
● Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)
● Secreted by the fetal (primitive) cortex
● Converted to estrogen by the placenta to maintain pregnancy.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Describe the signaling mechanism that regulates the specification and migration of neural crest cells into the adrenal medulla.
back:
● Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs)
● Secreted by the dorsal aorta
● Act as chemoattractants and differentiation signals for chromaffin precursors.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Contrast the embryonic origins of the two primary components of the adrenal gland.
back:
● Adrenal Cortex: Mesoderm (mesothelial cells near the urogenital ridge)
● Adrenal Medulla: Ectoderm (neural crest cells).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Outline the two distinct 'waves' of mesothelial proliferation that form the adrenal cortex.
back:
● First wave: Large acidophilic cells forming the fetal (primitive) cortex
● Second wave: Smaller cells forming the definitive cortex
● Occurs during the 5th and 6th weeks of development.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: During the [___] week of development, mesothelial cells between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad begin proliferating to form the fetal cortex.
back:
● Fifth (5th) week
● Proliferation occurs in the posterior abdominal wall mesoderm
● Cells penetrate the underlying mesenchyme.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: An infant is diagnosed with an adrenal tumor arising from cells that stain yellow-brown with chrome salts. Identify the embryonic source and clinical name of these cells.
back:
● Chromaffin cells
● Derived from Neural Crest cells
● Tumors of these cells are called Pheochromocytomas.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: How do the definitive layers of the adrenal cortex organize postnatally from the second mesothelial wave?
back:
● Fetal cortex regresses rapidly after birth
● Remaining cells differentiate into three zones
● Order: Zona glomerulosa, fasciculata, and reticularis.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Distinguish between the fate of the fetal cortex and the definitive cortex in the first year of life.
back:
● Fetal Cortex: Undergoes rapid involution and regression
● Definitive Cortex: Persists and organizes into the adult tripartite structure.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Identify the specific location where mesothelial cells proliferate to initiate adrenal cortical development.
back:
● Between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad
● Within the urogenital ridge
● Posterior abdominal wall.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Embryological origin of the adrenal cortex
front: The adrenal cortex primarily originates from the [___] located between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad.
back:
• Mesoderm (mesothelial cells)
• Proliferation begins in the fifth week
• Forms the acidophilic fetal cortex initially

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A 30-year-old presents with paroxysmal hypertension and tachycardia. Imaging reveals an adrenal medullary tumor. Identify the embryological cell type and its origin.
back:
• Chromaffin cells
• Derived from Neural Crest cells (ectoderm)
• Represent modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Explain the role of the fetal adrenal cortex in sustaining pregnancy during the second trimester.
back:
• Secretes Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA)
• DHEA is converted to estrogen by the placenta
• Estrogen maintains the placenta and pregnancy

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Contrast the fetal (primitive) cortex with the definitive cortex regarding their developmental waves and postnatal fate.
back:
• Fetal: 1st wave (acidophilic cells); regresses rapidly after birth
• Definitive: 2nd wave (smaller cells); persists and forms adult layers

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Specify the signaling molecules and their source that regulate the migration of neural crest cells into the adrenal medulla.
back:
• Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs)
• Secreted by the dorsal aorta
• Act as chemoattractants and specification factors

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: The adult histological zones of the adrenal cortex are derived from the [___] wave of mesothelial cells.
back:
• Second wave (Definitive cortex)
• Surrounds the original fetal cortex
• Differentiates postnatally into three layers

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A neonate's adrenal gland is disproportionately large at birth but undergoes rapid size reduction within weeks. Identify the histological structure regressing.
back:
• Fetal (primitive) cortex
• Regresses as the definitive cortex differentiates
• Adult zones (glomerulosa, fasciculata, reticularis) form

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Describe the functional mechanism that allows chromaffin cells to release catecholamines directly into the bloodstream.
back:
• Function as postganglionic sympathetic neurons lacking axons
• Stimulated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers
• Release epinephrine and norepinephrine as hormones

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Contrast the embryological 'parent' tissues of the adrenal cortex versus the adrenal medulla.
back:
• Cortex: Mesothelial mesoderm (urogenital ridge)
• Medulla: Ectodermal neural crest cells
• Fusion occurs as crest cells invade mesoderm

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: List the three definitive layers of the adrenal cortex in order from superficial to deep.
back:
• Zona glomerulosa
• Zona fasciculata
• Zona reticularis
• (Derived from the definitive cortex wave)

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Primordial germ cells (PGCs) originate in the [___] during the third week before migrating to the yolk sac wall.
back:
• Epiblast
• Migrate through the primitive streak
• Eventually reach the genital ridges in the 6th week

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A research embryo exhibits a complete failure of primordial germ cells to migrate into the genital ridges. State the primary developmental outcome.
back:
• Gonads fail to develop
• PGCs exert a mandatory inductive influence on gonadal formation

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain how the longitudinal genital (gonadal) ridges are initially formed on the medial side of the mesonephros.
back:
• Proliferation of surface epithelium
• Condensation of underlying mesenchyme

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the structural fate of primitive sex cords in male vs. female embryos as they move beyond the indifferent stage.
back:
• Male: Proliferate and penetrate deep to form testis (medullary) cords
• Female: Dissociate into irregular clusters and disappear; replaced by vascular stroma (ovarian medulla)

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Identify the critical week of development when the gonads first acquire distinct male or female morphological characteristics.
back: • Seventh week of development

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: During the indifferent stage, both sexes possess [___], which are connected to the surface epithelium and penetrate the underlying mesenchyme.
back: • Primitive sex cords

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: An embryo at the 4th week shows cells migrating by ameboid movement along the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut. Identify the cell type and their destination.
back:
• Cell type: Primordial germ cells (PGCs)
• Destination: Primitive gonads (genital ridges)

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: How do the primitive sex cords form within the indifferent gonad?
back:
• Surface epithelium proliferates
• Epithelial cells penetrate the underlying mesenchyme to form irregular cords

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Distinguish the anatomical location of primordial germ cells at the 3rd week versus the 6th week of development.
back:
• 3rd week: Wall of the yolk sac (near the allantois)
• 6th week: Invading the genital ridges

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Define the anatomical reason why the gonad is termed 'indifferent' prior to the 7th week.
back:
• Absence of male or female morphological characteristics
• Primitive sex cords are connected to surface epithelium in both sexes

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: The primordial germ cells, which eventually populate the indifferent gonads, first originate in the [___] during the second week of development.
back:
● Epiblast
● Migrate through primitive streak
● Reside in yolk sac wall by week 3
● Essential for gonadal induction

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A research embryo is noted to have a failure of primordial germ cell migration into the gonadal ridges. Identify the likely developmental outcome for the gonads.
back:
● Gonadal Agenesis
● Failure of ridges to differentiate
● Ridges remain rudimentary
● Migration typically occurs by week 6

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Describe the anatomical pathway through which primordial germ cells migrate from the yolk sac to the indifferent gonadal ridges.
back:
● Ameboid movement
● Along dorsal mesentery
● Passes through hindgut region
● Arrives at ridges by week 5

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the 'genital ridge' and the 'mesonephric ridge' in terms of their anatomical relationship and final derivatives.
back:
● Genital Ridge: Medial position; forms gonads
● Mesonephric Ridge: Lateral position; forms urinary structures
● Urogenital Ridge: Combined structure attached to posterior wall

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: List the two primary tissue components that proliferate to form the longitudinal genital ridges during the indifferent stage.
back:
● Surface epithelium (mesodermal)
● Underlying condensed mesenchyme
● Appears as longitudinal ridges
● Formed on medial mesonephros

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: In the indifferent gonad, the proliferating surface epithelium penetrates the underlying mesenchyme to form the [___].
back:
● Primitive sex cords
● Irregularly shaped cell clusters
● Remain connected to surface
● Common to both sexes

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A 46,XY embryo is analyzed at 6 weeks of gestation. Despite the genetic sex, why is the gonad still classified as 'indifferent' at this specific time?
back:
● No morphological sexual dimorphism
● Sex cords still connected to surface
● Testis-specific traits appear at week 7
● SRY cascade not yet visibly manifested

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain the biological necessity of the SRY gene in transitioning the indifferent gonad into a testis.
back:
● Encodes Testis-Determining Factor (TDF)
● Stimulates medullary cord proliferation
● Promotes Tunica Albuginea formation
● Inhibits cortical cord development

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Distinguish between the fate of primitive sex cords in an XX vs. an XY indifferent gonad during early differentiation.
back:
● XY: Cords persist/proliferate (Medullary cords)
● XX: Cords dissociate into clusters (Regress)
● XX: Replaced by vascular stroma
● XX: Cortical cords develop later

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Identify the critical week of development by which the indifferent gonad first acquires recognizable male or female morphological characteristics.
back:
● Seventh Week
● Before this: Indifferent stage
● Week 6: PGC invasion completed
● Week 7: TDF influence begins

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: Definition and Origin of Genital Ridges
front: The indifferent gonads initially appear as longitudinal elevations called [___], formed by the proliferation of surface epithelium and condensation of underlying mesenchyme.
back:
• Genital (or gonadal) ridges.
• Formed during the 5th week of development.
• Located on the medial side of the mesonephros.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: Inductive Role of Primordial Germ Cells
front: An embryo exhibits genital ridges, but primordial germ cells fail to migrate from the yolk sac. Predict the consequence for gonadal development.
back:
• Gonads will not develop.
• Primordial germ cells (PGCs) have a mandatory inductive influence on the genital ridge.
• Without PGCs, the indifferent gonad remains vestigial or fails to differentiate.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Describe the mechanism by which primitive sex cords are formed during the indifferent stage of gonadal development.
back:
• Surface epithelium of the genital ridge proliferates.
• Epithelial cells penetrate the underlying mesenchyme.
• They form irregularly shaped cords that remain connected to the surface epithelium.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: Dual Cellular Origin of Indifferent Gonads
front: Contrast the embryonic origin and migration route of primordial germ cells with the cells of the primitive sex cords.
back:
• PGCs: Arise in epiblast, migrate through yolk sac wall and hindgut mesentery.
• Sex Cords: Derived locally from the proliferation of surface epithelium of the genital ridge.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Identify the specific timeframe during which human gonads are morphologically indistinguishable between males and females.
back:
• From the 5th week until the 7th week of development.
• Sexual dimorphism (testis or ovary characteristics) only appears during the 7th week.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: Migration Path of Primordial Germ Cells
front: Primordial germ cells migrate from the wall of the [___] near the allantois to invade the genital ridges by the 6th week.
back:
• Yolk sac.
• Migration occurs via ameboid movement.
• Route follows the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A histological section of a 6-week embryo reveals a urogenital ridge. Which structure is located immediately lateral to the developing indifferent gonad?
back:
• The mesonephros.
• Both are attached to the posterior abdominal wall by the urogenital mesentery.
• The combined elevation is the urogenital ridge.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain why the gonad is termed 'indifferent' during the 6th week of gestation despite the genetic sex being determined at fertilization.
back:
• Genetic sex is determined by XY/XX at fertilization.
• Morphological sex (testis vs. ovary) is not apparent until the 7th week.
• Histology is identical in both sexes before this point.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Distinguish between the two main tissue processes that initiate the formation of the genital ridges.
back:
• Proliferation of the surface epithelium.
• Condensation of the underlying mesenchyme.
• This creates the longitudinal ridge medial to the mesonephros.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Specify the fate of the connection between the primitive sex cords and the surface epithelium in the indifferent stage.
back:
• In the indifferent stage, they remain connected to the surface.
• This connection persists until sex-specific differentiation (e.g., tunica albuginea formation in males) occurs.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: Timeline of Primordial Germ Cell Migration
front: The primordial germ cells, which exert a mandatory inductive influence on gonadal development, first invade the genital ridges during the [___] week of embryonic life.
back:
• Sixth week.
• Arrive via the dorsal mesentery of the hindgut.
• If they fail to reach the ridges, the gonads do not develop.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A histological study of an indifferent gonad in a 6-week embryo reveals failure of the surface epithelium to penetrate the underlying mesenchyme. Identify the specific structures that will fail to form.
back:
• Primitive sex cords.
• These are irregularly shaped cords that must connect to the surface epithelium in the indifferent stage.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain the biological contribution of the intermediate mesoderm to the formation of the 'urogenital ridge' in the second month of development.
back:
• Forms a longitudinal ridge on the posterior abdominal wall.
• Gives rise to the mesonephros laterally.
• Gives rise to the genital/gonadal ridge medially via epithelial proliferation.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the morphological fate of the medullary cords in a 46,XX embryo versus a 46,XY embryo during the transition from the indifferent stage.
back:
• 46,XY (Male): Medullary cords persist and differentiate into testis/medullary cords.
• 46,XX (Female): Medullary cords dissociate into irregular clusters and eventually disappear/regress.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
coreConcept: SRY Gene Influence on Indifferent Gonads
front: Describe the specific genetic trigger required to prevent the indifferent gonad from following the default pathway of ovarian differentiation.
back:
• SRY (Sex-determining region on Y) gene expression.
• Encodes Testis-Determining Factor (TDF).
• Initiates the cascade for medullary cord development and Tunica Albuginea formation.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Germ layer origin of adrenal cortex
front: The adrenal cortex originates from the [___] germ layer, specifically from the mesothelial cells between the root of the mesentery and the developing gonad.
back:
Mesoderm.
- Proliferation begins in the 5th week.
- Forms both the fetal (primitive) and definitive cortex.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Fetal Adrenal Cortex Fate and Function
front: A 1-week-old neonate shows rapid involution of the innermost layer of the adrenal gland. Identify this transient structure and its primary secretion during the second trimester.
back:
Fetal (Primitive) Cortex.
- Secretes Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA).
- DHEA is converted to estrogen by the placenta.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Explain the biological mechanism by which the adrenal medulla forms from its parent cells.
back:
Neural crest cells invade the medial aspect of the fetal cortex.
- They arrange into cords and clusters.
- Differentiate into chromaffin cells (modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A neonate presents with excessive androgenization. Differentiate the 'fetal' and 'definitive' cortical waves in terms of their physical characteristics and timing.
back:
Fetal Cortex (1st Wave):
- Large acidophilic cells; 5th week.
- Regresses after birth.
Definitive Cortex (2nd Wave):
- Small mesothelial cells; surround fetal mass.
- Forms Glomerulosa, Fasciculata, and Reticularis.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Identify the chemical markers and functional classification of the cells forming the adrenal medulla.
back:
Chromaffin cells.
- Stain yellow-brown with chrome salts.
- Classified as modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: The migration of neural crest cells to the adrenal medulla is primarily regulated by [___] secreted by the dorsal aorta.
back:
Bone Morphogenetic Proteins (BMPs).
- Act as chemoattractants for migrating crest cells.
- Regulate differentiation into chromaffin tissue.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A 30-year-old patient presents with paroxysmal hypertension and tachycardia due to a chromaffin cell tumor. Trace the embryological origin of the affected tissue.
back:
Neural Crest (Ectoderm).
- Tumor is a Pheochromocytoma.
- Arises from medullary tissue that failed to differentiate or became neoplastic.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Explain the role of the fetal adrenal cortex in maintaining the maternal-fetal unit during pregnancy.
back:
Produces DHEA (Dehydroepiandrosterone).
- Placenta converts DHEA into estrogen.
- Estrogen is essential for maintaining the pregnancy and placental health.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Contrast the adrenal cortex and medulla regarding their embryological parentage and secreted products.
back:
Cortex (Mesoderm):
- Secretes Steroids (Cortisol, Aldosterone, Androgens).
Medulla (Ectoderm/Neural Crest):
- Secretes Catecholamines (Epinephrine, Norepinephrine).

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: List the three definitive layers of the adrenal cortex in their chronological order of postnatal differentiation.
back:
1. Zona Glomerulosa.
2. Zona Fasciculata.
3. Zona Reticularis.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
coreConcept: Germ Layer Origins of Adrenal Gland
front: The adrenal cortex originates from the [___] germ layer, while the medulla is derived from neural crest cells.
back:
• Mesoderm (specifically mesothelial cells).
• Forms between the root of the mesentery and the urogenital ridge.
• Proliferation begins during the 5th week.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A genetic female infant presents with ambiguous genitalia. Labs reveal an enzyme deficiency leading to excessive androgen production by the adrenal primordium. Identify the specific part of the gland responsible.
back:
• Adrenal Cortex.
• Specifically, the definitive cortex fails to regulate androgens in Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia.
• Leads to virilization due to cortisol synthesis blocks.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Explain the specific biochemical role of the fetal adrenal cortex in maintaining the hormonal environment of pregnancy.
back:
• Secretes DHEA (dehydroepiandrosterone).
• DHEA is converted to estrogen by the placenta.
• Essential for maintaining placental function and the pregnancy state.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A 35-year-old experiences paroxysmal hypertension and tachycardia. Imaging shows a tumor in the adrenal medulla. This tumor originates from which embryonic cell population?
back:
• Neural crest cells.
• These migrate and differentiate into chromaffin cells.
• The condition is Pheochromocytoma, involving catecholamine-secreting cells.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Describe the developmental transformation of neural crest cells once they invade the medial aspect of the fetal adrenal cortex.
back:
• Differentiate into chromaffin cells.
• Form the adrenal medulla.
• Act as modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons without axons.
• Secrete epinephrine and norepinephrine directly into blood.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Following the postnatal regression of the fetal cortex, the definitive adrenal cortex organizes into three layers: the zona glomerulosa, the zona fasciculata, and the [___].
back:
• Zona reticularis.
• Fetal cortex regresses rapidly after birth.
• Definitive layers specialize in aldosterone, cortisol, and androgen secretion.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: A newborn is found to have an adrenal gland where the fetal cortex has failed to regress. How does the size of this fetal cortex normally compare to the adult gland at birth?
back:
• Large/Massive.
• The adrenal gland at birth is disproportionately large due to the extensive fetal cortex.
• Regression occurs shortly after birth.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: How do signaling molecules from the dorsal aorta influence the migration and specification of the adrenal medulla?
back:
• Secretes BMPs (Bone Morphogenetic Proteins).
• BMPs act as chemoattractants for neural crest cells.
• Directs migration toward the adrenal primordium and regulates medullary lineage.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Contrast the fetal adrenal cortex with the definitive cortex regarding their waves of formation.
back:
• Fetal Cortex: First wave of mesothelial cells; large acidophilic cells.
• Definitive Cortex: Second wave of mesothelial cells; smaller cells surrounding the fetal core.

category: Identify the stages in the development of the adrenal gland
front: Identify the primary source of cells that form the definitive adrenal cortex.
back:
• Mesothelium (Mesoderm).
• Proliferates as a second wave of cells during the fetal period.
• Surrounds the primary/fetal acidophilic cell mass.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Primordial germ cells originate in the [___] during the third week of development before migrating to the wall of the yolk sac.
back:
• Epiblast
• Move via the primitive streak
• Reside near the allantois in the yolk sac

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A fetus fails to develop gonads despite a normal karyotype. This is most likely due to a failure in the ameboid migration of cells along the [___] during the fourth and fifth weeks.
back:
• Dorsal mesentery of the hindgut
• Refers to Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs)
• PGCs have an essential inductive influence

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain the role of the coelomic epithelium in the formation of the indifferent gonad.
back:
• Proliferates into underlying mesenchyme
• Forms the primitive sex cords
• Remains connected to surface in indifferent stage

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the fate of medullary cords in XX embryos versus XY embryos during gonadal differentiation.
back:
• XY: Develop into testis cords/medullary cords
• XX: Dissociate into irregular clusters and regress
• Ovarian medulla eventually becomes vascular stroma

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Identify the genetic transcription factor that acts as the 'master switch' for initiating the transition from an indifferent gonad to a testis.
back:
• SRY protein (Testis-determining factor)
• Encoded on the short arm of the Y chromosome (Yp11)

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: The 'urogenital ridge' is the embryological structure formed by the proliferation of mesenchyme and epithelium on the [___] side of the mesonephros.
back:
• Medial side
• Components: Genital ridge + Mesonephros

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A histology slide of a 6-week embryo shows gonads containing both primitive sex cords and primordial germ cells, yet male and female features are indistinguishable. Name this specific developmental phase.
back:
• Indifferent stage of the gonad
• Lasts until the 7th week of development

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Describe the physiological consequence if primordial germ cells fail to reach the genital ridges by the sixth week.
back:
• Gonads do not develop
• Resulting in 'streak gonads' or gonadal agenesis
• Loss of inductive stimulus for sex cord development

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Distinguish between the 1st and 2nd generations of sex cords in female gonadal development.
back:
• 1st (Primitive): Form medullary cords (regress)
• 2nd (Cortical): Form in 7th week; surround oogonia to form follicles

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: By which week of intrauterine life do primordial germ cells typically invade the genital ridges?
back:
• Sixth week
• (Arrive at primitive gonads at the start of the 5th week)

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: During the 4th week, primordial germ cells migrate from the yolk sac wall toward the genital ridges by moving along the [___].
back:
• Dorsal mesentery of the hindgut.
• They arrive at the primitive gonads by the 5th week.
• They invade the genital ridges by the 6th week.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: An embryo fails to have primordial germ cells (PGCs) reach the genital ridges during the 6th week of development. Predict the effect on gonadal development.
back:
• The gonads fail to develop (gonadal agenesis).
• PGCs exert a mandatory inductive influence on the development of the indifferent gonad into ovaries or testes.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Explain the biological formation of the 'primitive sex cords' during the indifferent stage of gonadal development.
back:
• Surface epithelium of the genital ridge proliferates.
• Epithelial cells penetrate the underlying mesenchyme.
• Irregularly shaped cords are formed, remaining connected to the surface epithelium.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Contrast the anatomical components of the 'urogenital ridge' with the 'genital (gonadal) ridge' in a 6-week embryo.
back:
• Urogenital Ridge: Large ovoid organ formed by both the mesonephros and the developing gonad.
• Genital Ridge: The specific medial thickening of the urogenital ridge derived from epithelium and mesenchyme.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Identify the specific gestational week when gonads first acquire distinct male or female morphological characteristics.
back:
• 7th week of development.
• Before this, the gonad is morphologically 'indifferent' despite genetic sex being determined at fertilization (XY or XX).

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: The indifferent gonad is formed by the proliferation of [___] and the condensation of the underlying mesenchyme.
back:
• Surface epithelium (coelomic epithelium).
• This occurs on the medial side of the mesonephros within the urogenital ridge.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: A 6-week embryo is genetically 46,XY. Histology of the gonad shows primitive sex cords connected to surface epithelium. Why can sex not be determined morphologically yet?
back:
• The gonad is in the 'indifferent stage'.
• SRY-mediated differentiation into medullary (testis) cords only becomes visible starting in the 7th week.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Detail the migratory sequence of Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs) from their origin to the genital ridge invasion.
back:
• Origin: Epiblast.
• 3rd Week: Yolk sac wall near allantois.
• 4th Week: Ameboid movement along hindgut dorsal mesentery.
• 6th Week: Invasion of genital ridges.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Distinguish between the two pairs of genital ducts present in both sexes during the indifferent stage.
back:
• Mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts: Existing urinary ducts utilized by the male system.
• Paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts: Longitudinal invaginations of the coelomic epithelium on the urogenital ridge.

category: Describe the indifferent gonads
front: Specify the precise anatomical location of the genital ridges and their attachment to the abdominal wall.
back:
• Location: Medial side of the mesonephros.
• Attachment: Posterior abdominal wall via a broad urogenital mesentery.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The master gene located on the short arm of the Y chromosome that acts as the primary transcription factor switch for male sex determination is [___].
back:
• SRY (Sex-determining Region on Y) gene.
• Produces testis-determining factor.
• Initiates a cascade of downstream genes for male development.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A 46,XY phenotypic female presents with streak gonads. DNA analysis shows a loss-of-function mutation in the SRY gene. Explain the gonadal outcome.
back:
• Failure of testis differentiation.
• In the absence of SRY, the medullary cords regress.
• The default female pathway is established despite the XY karyotype.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the role of WNT4 and DAX1 in the molecular regulation of ovarian differentiation.
back:
• WNT4 acts as the ovary-determining gene.
• It upregulates DAX1.
• DAX1 actively inhibits SOX9 expression, preventing the male pathway and promoting ovarian development.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Contrast the developmental fate of primitive sex cords in male embryos versus female embryos.
back:
• Males: Continue proliferating to form medullary (testis) cords.
• Females: Dissociate into irregular cell clusters that regress and are replaced by vascular stroma (medulla).

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Identify the specific transcription factor that, when upregulated by SOX9, stimulates the differentiation of both Sertoli and Leydig cells.
back:
• Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1).
• Elevates Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) in Sertoli cells.
• Upregulates testosterone synthesis enzymes in Leydig cells.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Primordial germ cells must reach the genital ridges by the sixth week of development to exert a mandatory [___] influence on gonad differentiation.
back:
• Inductive influence.
• If germ cells fail to arrive, gonads remain indifferent or do not develop at all.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: An embryo is found to have absent Sertoli cells but normal Leydig cell function. Predict the effect on the internal ductal system.
back:
• Persistence of Müllerian (paramesonephric) ducts.
• Lack of Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) prevents ductal regression.
• Wolffian ducts still develop due to Leydig cell testosterone.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Describe the formation and timing of the cortical cords during ovarian development.
back:
• Arise from surface epithelium in the 7th week.
• Form a secondary generation of cords.
• Split into isolated clusters (primordial follicles) in the 3rd month.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Distinguish between the signaling roles of Testosterone and Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) in male genital development.
back:
• Testosterone: Stimulates mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts to form the epididymis and vas deferens.
• DHT: Mediates the differentiation of male external genitalia (penis and scrotum).

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Identify the anatomical landmarks where the gonads first appear before acquiring male or female characteristics.
back:
• Genital or gonadal ridges.
• Formed by proliferation of surface epithelium and condensation of underlying mesenchyme.
• Located on the medial side of the mesonephros.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The master gene for testis determination, located on the short arm of the Y chromosome, is the [___] gene.
back:
• SRY (Sex-determining Region on Y)
• Encodes a transcription factor
• Initiates a cascade for male differentiation
• Acts in conjunction with SOX9

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: An infant with a 46,XY karyotype is born with female external genitalia. Point mutations in the SRY gene are confirmed. Identify the likely diagnosis and underlying mechanism.
back:
• Swyer Syndrome (Pure Gonadal Dysgenesis)
• SRY failure prevents SOX9 activation
• Medullary cords fail to develop into testis
• Gonads remain as non-functional streak gonads

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain how SOX9 carries out its biological function in the male gonadal ridge.
back:
• Binds to the AMH (Anti-Mullerian Hormone) promoter
• Stimulates Sertoli and Leydig cell differentiation
• Acts via SF1 (Steroidogenesis Factor 1)
• Upregulates FGF9 for mesonephric tubule penetration

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Contrast the molecular antagonism between DAX1 and SOX9 during sexual differentiation.
back:
• Males: SRY/SOX9 inhibit WNT4/DAX1 expression
• Females: WNT4 upregulates DAX1
• DAX1 actively inhibits SOX9 function
• Absence of SOX9 allows ovarian development

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Identify the specific role of Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1) in male gonadal development.
back:
• Works with SOX9 to elevate AMH/MIS
• Induces differentiation of Sertoli cells
• Induces differentiation of Leydig cells
• Upregulates genes for testosterone synthesis enzymes

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The primary 'ovary-determining gene' that upregulates DAX1 to inhibit male-specific pathways is [___].
back:
• WNT4
• Essential for ovarian differentiation
• Counteracts SOX9 activity via DAX1
• Leads to formation of secondary cortical cords

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A 16-year-old female presents with primary amenorrhea and a 46,XY karyotype. Laboratory tests reveal normal testosterone but a total lack of Anti-Mullerian Hormone (AMH). What is the developmental consequence?
back:
• Persistent Mullerian Duct Syndrome
• Paramesonephric ducts fail to regress
• Uterus and uterine tubes develop in a male
• Caused by Sertoli cell or AMH receptor defects

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the inductive role of Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs) upon the indifferent gonad.
back:
• PGCs must reach genital ridges by week 6
• They exert an essential inductive influence
• Absence results in gonadal agenesis
• Gonads remain as 'streak' tissue without PGCs

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Distinguish between the fate of Primitive Sex Cords in males versus females.
back:
• Males: Persist as Medullary (Testis) Cords
• Females: Dissociate; replaced by vascular stroma (medulla)
• Females: Secondary 'Cortical Cords' form from surface epithelium
• Males: Tunica albuginea separates cords from surface

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Name the specific hormone derivative and enzyme responsible for the differentiation of male external genitalia.
back:
• Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
• Produced by 5-alpha reductase enzyme
• Converts testosterone in target tissues
• Mediates growth of penis, scrotum, and prostate

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The key to sexual dimorphism is the Y chromosome, which contains the [___] gene on its short arm, acting as the master switch for testis differentiation.
back:
• SRY (Sex-determining Region on Y)
• Encodes testis-determining factor
• Initiates a cascade of downstream genes to determine male sex.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: An XY individual presents with female external genitalia and a lack of secondary sexual characteristics. Analysis reveals a point mutation on the short arm of the Y chromosome. Identify the likely target and its significance.
back:
• Target: SRY gene
• Result: Failure of testis-determining factor
• Outcome: Development of streak gonads and a female phenotype (Swyer Syndrome).

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the role of the SRY protein in initiating the differentiation of Sertoli and Leydig cells within the primitive gonad.
back:
• SRY upregulates SOX9 expression
• SOX9 and SRY induce Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1)
• SF1 stimulates differentiation of Sertoli and Leydig cells from gonadal mesenchyme.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Contrast the specific hormonal requirements for the persistence of mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts versus the regression of paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts in the male fetus.
back:
• Mesonephric Persistence: Requires Testosterone (secreted by Leydig cells)
• Paramesonephric Regression: Requires Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH/MIS) (secreted by Sertoli cells)
• Absence of these leads to female ductal development.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Identify the master ovary-determining gene and the specific nuclear receptor it upregulates to suppress the male developmental pathway.
back:
• Master Gene: WNT4
• Upregulated Receptor: DAX1
• Mechanism: DAX1 inhibits the function of the male-promoting SOX9 gene.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: If [___] fail to reach the genital ridges during the sixth week of development, the gonads will not develop into ovaries or testes.
back:
• Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs)
• Originate in the epiblast
• Provide essential inductive influence for gonadal maturation.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A 46,XY infant presents with ambiguous external genitalia but normal development of the epididymis and vas deferens. Explain the enzymatic deficiency responsible for this presentation.
back:
• 5-alpha reductase deficiency
• Internal ducts develop via Testosterone
• External genitalia fail to masculinize due to lack of Dihydrotestosterone (DHT).

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: How do the primitive sex cords differentiate differently in males compared to their fate in female embryos?
back:
• Males: Proliferate into medullary/testis cords connected to the hilum
• Females: Dissociate into cell clusters that eventually regress and are replaced by cortical cords.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Distinguish between the adult derivatives of the paramesonephric ducts in females and those of the mesonephric ducts in males.
back:
• Paramesonephric: Uterine tubes, uterus, cervix, and upper vagina
• Mesonephric: Epididymis, ductus deferens, ejaculatory duct, and seminal vesicles.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: State the timing (gestational week) when the indifferent gonad first acquires definitive male or female morphological characteristics.
back:
• Seventh week of development
• Prior to this, gonads appear as identical longitudinal genital ridges
• Differentiation depends on the presence of the SRY gene.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: The [___] wing of the third pharyngeal pouch is the specific embryonic site that differentiates into the inferior parathyroid gland.
back:
* **Dorsal wing** of the 3rd pouch.
* The ventral wing forms the thymus.
* Migration of the thymus pulls this gland to its final inferior position.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: A newborn presents with tetany and a missing thymic shadow on X-ray. The developmental failure of which pouches explains the lack of parathyroid glands in this patient?
back:
* **3rd and 4th Pharyngeal Pouches**.
* Diagnosis: DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 deletion).
* Results in aplasia of both thymus and parathyroid glands.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: Explain the role of the thymus in determining the final anatomical position of the inferior parathyroid glands.
back:
* **Migration Guide**: The thymus (3rd pouch) migrates caudally to the thorax.
* **Traction**: It pulls the inferior parathyroids along its migratory path.
* **Result**: They settle lower than the 4th pouch derivatives.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: Contrast the embryonic origins of the superior and inferior parathyroid glands in terms of their respective pharyngeal pouches.
back:
* **Superior**: 4th pharyngeal pouch (dorsal wing).
* **Inferior**: 3rd pharyngeal pouch (dorsal wing).
* **Clinical Note**: Despite the numbering, 3rd pouch glands migrate lower than 4th pouch glands.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: Identify the non-parathyroid structure derived from the ventral 4th pharyngeal pouch that integrates into the thyroid gland.
back:
* **Ultimobranchial Body**.
* Gives rise to **Parafollicular (C) cells**.
* These cells produce calcitonin to regulate blood calcium levels.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: Ectopic parathyroid tissue found at the bifurcation of the common carotid artery is most likely a remnant of the [___] pharyngeal pouch.
back:
* **3rd Pharyngeal Pouch**.
* Follows the descent path of the thymus.
* Accessory glands may persist anywhere along this migratory route.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
coreConcept: Neural Crest Contribution to Endocrine Glands
front: A patient is diagnosed with DiGeorge Syndrome. Failure of which specific cell population to populate the pharyngeal arches leads to the absence of the parathyroid stroma?
back:
* **Neural Crest Cells**.
* They provide the essential mesenchyme for the gland.
* Interaction between endoderm and neural crest is required for differentiation.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: How do the superior parathyroid glands reach their definitive location on the dorsal surface of the thyroid?
back:
* They lose connection with the **pharyngeal wall**.
* They attach to the **caudally migrating thyroid**.
* They remain fixed to the superior pole of the thyroid lobes.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: Distinguish between the 3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches based on their ventral wing derivatives.
back:
* **3rd Pouch Ventral**: Differentiates into the Thymus.
* **4th Pouch Ventral**: Differentiates into the Ultimobranchial Body.
* Both involve significant caudal migration during the 5th week.

category: Describe the development of para-thyroid glands
front: Name the primary germ layer that lines the pharyngeal pouches and forms the secretory cells of the parathyroid glands.
back:
* **Endoderm**.
* It forms the epithelial lining of all pharyngeal pouches.
* The endoderm eventually differentiates into the chief and oxyphil cells.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The master gene for male sexual dimorphism, located on the short arm of the Y chromosome (Yp11), is the [___] gene.
back:
The SRY (Sex-determining Region on Y) gene.
- Encodes Testis-Determining Factor (TDF).
- Initiates a cascade of downstream genes for male gonadal fate.
- In its absence, female development is established.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A phenotypic female presents with primary amenorrhea and a 46,XY karyotype. MRI shows 'streak gonads.' Point mutations or deletions in [___] likely caused this failure of gonadal differentiation.
back:
The SRY gene.
- Leads to Swyer Syndrome (XY Gonadal Dysgenesis).
- Prevents the indifferent gonad from differentiating into a testis.
- Results in regression of germ cells into fibrous 'streak' tissue.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the essential role of Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs) in the morphological development of the gonads.
back:
PGCs exert an inductive influence on differentiation.
- Arrive at genital ridges by the 6th week.
- If PGCs fail to reach the ridges, gonads do not develop.
- Resulting gonads remain 'indifferent' or are completely absent.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Contrast the developmental fate of the primitive sex cords in male versus female embryos.
back:
Male (XY):
- Cords proliferate to form medullary (testis) cords.
- Separated from epithelium by tunica albuginea.

Female (XX):
- Primitive medullary cords dissociate and disappear.
- Replaced by secondary 'cortical cords.'

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
coreConcept: Role of SF1 in Gonadal Differentiation
front: Identify the transcription factor upregulated by SRY that stimulates the specific differentiation of both Sertoli and Leydig cells.
back:
Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1).
- Works with SOX9 to elevate Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) in Sertoli cells.
- Upregulates enzymes in Leydig cells for testosterone synthesis.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: In the absence of the Y chromosome, the ovary-determining master gene [___] is expressed to regulate female differentiation.
back:
WNT4.
- Upregulates DAX1 to inhibit SOX9 function.
- Downstream targets like TAFII105 induce ovarian follicular development.
- Absence of this pathway prevents normal ovarian formation.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A newborn is diagnosed with an ovotesticular disorder of sex development (true hermaphroditism). Pathophysiologically, this involves the simultaneous presence of [___].
back:
Both ovarian and testicular tissue.
- May present as an 'ovotestis' or separate ovary/testis.
- Usually associated with 46,XX karyotype (70%).
- Ambiguous external genitalia with a tendency toward masculinization.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: How do SRY and SOX9 utilize Fibroblast Growth Factor 9 (FGF9) to ensure testis differentiation continues?
back:
FGF9 acts as a chemotactic factor.
- Causes tubules from the mesonephric duct to penetrate the gonadal ridge.
- Essential for forming the network required for medullary cord maturation.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Distinguish the microscopic barrier that forms in the male gonad at 8 weeks but is characteristically absent in the female gonad.
back:
Tunica Albuginea.
- A dense layer of fibrous connective tissue.
- Separates testis cords from the surface epithelium.
- Its absence in females allows cortical cord proliferation.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: State the chronological migration path of Primordial Germ Cells from their origin to the primitive gonad.
back:
Epiblast → Primitive streak (week 3) → Yolk sac wall near allantois.
- Week 4: Move along hindgut dorsal mesentery via amoeboid movement.
- Week 5: Arrive at primitive gonads.
- Week 6: Invade genital ridges.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The master gene for testis differentiation, located on the short arm of the Y chromosome, is [___].
back:
SRY (Sex-determining region on Y) gene.
- Encodes Testis-determining factor.
- Initiates a cascade for male sexual dimorphism.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A phenotypically female patient presents with a 46,XY karyotype and streak gonads. Molecular analysis reveals a point mutation in the SRY gene. Name this condition.
back:
Swyer Syndrome (XY female gonadal dysgenesis).
- Result of failure of testis-determining factor.
- Leads to lack of secondary sexual characteristics at puberty.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the essential inductive role of Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs) in gonadal development.
back:
PGCs migrate from the yolk sac to the genital ridges by the 6th week.
- They exert an inductive influence on ridge differentiation.
- If PGCs fail to reach the ridges, the gonads do not develop.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Contrast the developmental fate of the primitive sex cords in male vs. female embryos.
back:
Males: Cords proliferate into medullary (testis) cords under SRY.
- Females: Primitive cords dissociate into cell clusters; secondary cortical cords form from surface epithelium.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Identify the dual downstream function of Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1) in male gonadal development.
back:
1. Works with SOX9 to elevate AMH (MIS) concentrations, regressing Müllerian ducts.
- 2. Upregulates enzymes in Leydig cells for testosterone synthesis.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: In female gonadal differentiation, the master ovary-determining gene is [___].
back:
WNT4.
- Upregulates DAX1 to inhibit SOX9.
- Regulates identify of identifying target genes (e.g., TAFII105).

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A male infant presents with a 46,XY karyotype, normal testes, and male external genitalia, yet possesses a uterus and uterine tubes. Identify the likely underlying molecular defect.
back:
Persistent Müllerian Duct Syndrome.
- Caused by deficiency of Müllerian Inhibiting Substance (MIS/AMH).
- Or due to a defect in AMH receptors.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Describe the mechanism by which the male gonad prevents the development of female internal reproductive structures.
back:
Sertoli cells produce AMH (Anti-Müllerian Hormone).
- AMH causes the regression of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts.
- This prevents the formation of the uterus and uterine tubes.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Distinguish between the hormonal requirements for the development of the Epididymis vs. the Scrotum.
back:
Epididymis: Requires Testosterone (stimulates mesonephric ducts).
- Scrotum: Requires Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) (via 5-alpha reductase conversion).

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Specify the germ layer origin of the gonadal (genital) ridges.
back:
Intermediate Mesoderm.
- Formed by proliferation of the epithelium and condensation of underlying mesenchyme.
- Located on the medial side of the mesonephros.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The master gene for male sex determination, SRY, is located on the [___] of the Y chromosome.
back: Short arm (specifically region Yp11). It encodes the testis-determining factor required to initiate the male developmental cascade.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
coreConcept: Inductive Influence of Primordial Germ Cells
front: A histological study of a 6-week human embryo reveals that primordial germ cells failed to migrate from the yolk sac to the genital ridges. Predict the effect on gonadal development.
back: The gonads will fail to develop. Primordial germ cells exert a mandatory inductive influence on the genital ridges; without their arrival, the indifferent gonad remains vestigial.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the molecular mechanism by which WNT4 promotes ovarian differentiation while actively suppressing the male pathway.
back: WNT4 upregulates DAX1, a member of the nuclear hormone receptor family. DAX1 specifically inhibits the function of SOX9, thereby preventing the male-determining cascade.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
coreConcept: FGF9 vs. SF1 in Testis Morphogenesis
front: Contrast the roles of FGF9 and Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1) in the early morphogenesis of the fetal testes.
back: FGF9: Acts as a chemotactic factor causing mesonephric tubules to penetrate the gonadal ridge. SF1: Upregulates enzymes for testosterone synthesis in Leydig cells and works with SOX9 to elevate AMH levels.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Describe the dual function of the SOX9 transcription factor in male sexual differentiation.
back: SOX9 binds the promoter region of the Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) gene to induce its expression and independently induces the differentiation of the testes even in some SRY-deficient contexts.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: The key master gene for male sexual dimorphism, located on the short arm of the Y chromosome and encoding the testis-determining factor, is [___].
back:
### SRY Gene
* Located at Yp11.
* Acts as a transcription factor for downstream male genes.
* In its absence, the female developmental pathway is established.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A 46,XY phenotypic female presents with primary amenorrhea and streak gonads. Genetic testing reveals a point mutation in the SRY gene. Name the condition.
back:
### Swyer Syndrome
* XY Pure Gonadal Dysgenesis.
* Failure of SRY prevents medullary cord development.
* Lack of AMH and testosterone leads to female phenotype despite XY genotype.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Explain the role of the WNT4 gene in the molecular regulation of ovarian differentiation.
back:
### WNT4 Function
* The primary ovary-determining gene.
* Upregulates DAX1, which inhibits the pro-testis gene SOX9.
* Promotes development of secondary cortical cords and identifies target genes like TAFII105.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Contrast the developmental fate of primitive sex cords in male versus female embryos during the transition from the indifferent stage.
back:
### Medullary vs. Cortical Cords
* **Males**: Primitive cords proliferate into medullary (testis) cords; cortical cords fail to develop.
* **Females**: Primitive cords dissociate and regress; secondary cortical cords form to surround oogonia.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Detail the function of Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1) in the male gonadal differentiation pathway.
back:
### Steroidogenesis Factor 1 (SF1)
* Stimulates differentiation of Sertoli and Leydig cells.
* Synergizes with SOX9 to increase AMH levels.
* Upregulates enzymes in Leydig cells for testosterone synthesis.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Gonadal development fails to occur entirely if the [___] do not invade the genital ridges by the sixth week of gestation.
back:
### Primordial Germ Cells (PGCs)
* Originate in the epiblast.
* Migrate from the yolk sac via the dorsal mesentery.
* Exert an essential inductive influence on gonadal differentiation.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: A 46,XY infant presents with normal male external genitalia, but a uterus and fallopian tubes are discovered during surgery for undescended testes. Identify the hormonal deficiency.
back:
### Persistent Müllerian Duct Syndrome
* Deficiency of Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH/MIS).
* Caused by Sertoli cell failure or AMH receptor mutation.
* Paramesonephric ducts fail to regress despite male hormonal signaling.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Describe the mechanism by which SOX9 causes the regression of Müllerian ducts in male embryos.
back:
### SOX9 and AMH Regulation
* SOX9 is upregulated by SRY protein.
* It binds directly to the promoter region of the Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) gene.
* Increased AMH causes regression of the paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Distinguish between the histological structure of the early testis and ovary based on the presence of the Tunica Albuginea.
back:
### Tunica Albuginea
* **Testis**: A dense layer of fibrous connective tissue that separates testis cords from surface epithelium.
* **Ovary**: Absent; surface epithelium remains proliferative to produce cortical cords.

category: List and describe the Factors influencing the differentiation of gonads
front: Specify the exact week of development when gonads first begin to acquire morphological male or female characteristics.
back:
### Seventh Week
* Prior to this, gonads are in the 'indifferent stage'.
* Morphological dimorphism begins under the influence of SRY or WNT4.

category: Evaluate the role of the factors influencing Sex determination and differentiation
front: The master gene for sexual dimorphism, located on the short arm of the Y chromosome, is the [___] gene.
back:
● SRY (Sex-determining Region on Y)
● Encodes Testis-Determining Factor (TDF)
● Initiates a cascade for male gonadal differentiation
● Acts by upregulating SOX9

category: Evaluate the role of the factors influencing Sex determination and differentiation
front: A phenotypic female presents with a short, blind-ending vagina, absent uterus, and bilateral undescended testes. Karyotype is 46,XY. Identify the most likely pathophysiology.
back:
● Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome (AIS)
● Lack of androgen receptors or response
● AMH from Sertoli cells still regresses Müllerian ducts
● Testosterone is ineffective at virilizing external genitalia

category: Evaluate the role of the factors influencing Sex determination and differentiation
front: Explain the mechanism by which paramesonephric (Müllerian) ducts are regressed in a male embryo.
back:
● Sertoli cells secrete Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH/MIS)
● AMH acts on paramesonephric ducts during early development
● Results in total duct regression except for the appendix testis
